digest.intro: Hidden infrastructure exposed, dead silicon cracked open, and a mouse that thinks with human cells.

items.title: Boston Dumps Flock After 'Vendor Error' Shared Data Nationwide
items.blurb: Boston's BPD explicitly disabled nationwide data-sharing in its Flock ALPR contract — and within three days of going live, other law enforcement agencies across the country could already query Boston's plates anyway. The city pulled the plug entirely. This is the policy consequence: when the default state of a surveillance platform is 'share everything,' a contract clause is not a firewall.

items.title: Open Chinese Models Are Four Months Behind Frontier AI at One-Fifth the Cost
items.blurb: Mozilla's new data puts a concrete number on the open/closed capability gap: paying for frontier proprietary AI currently buys you roughly a four-month lead, at five times the cost. The geopolitical implication is that the window in which US labs can claim meaningful capability superiority is compressing fast, and the leverage point is shifting from model intelligence to deployment infrastructure and data access.

sections.heading: Infrastructure you couldn't see until now

items.title: Hackers Ripped a Flock Camera Off a Pole and Read Its Brain
items.blurb: The encryption key that Flock promised protects on-device data was stored on the device itself — so once you have the hardware, you have the key. The dumped logs show the camera generating over a million images in a few weeks, tracking not just plates but people, bicycles, and bumper stickers including, specifically, an American flag patch on a motorcyclist's saddlebag. What Flock sold as a license-plate reader is behaviorally a general-purpose visual surveillance node.

items.title: Rheinmetall Open-Sources Its Battlefield Weapon Integration Protocol
items.blurb: A major European defense contractor just published its sensor-to-software integration API on GitHub — DDS publish-subscribe architecture, C++ core, wrappers for Python and Java, full data schema — as if it were an open-source middleware library for a logistics startup. The casual normalcy of the presentation is the strange part: military hardware interoperability specs, styled like a developer docs site you'd find for any SaaS tool.

items.title: Apple Builds Cryptographic Provenance Into the Shutter
items.blurb: Apple's approach goes further than the existing C2PA standard, which attaches provenance metadata after capture and can be tampered with anywhere downstream — instead, Apple anchors a reference image at the sensor level with a chain of trust that runs through the computational photography stack. Crucially, it's designed to work without tying an image to a photographer's public identity, which matters for anyone shooting in dangerous conditions. The authenticity question for photography just moved from 'can you tell?' to 'did the hardware witness it?'

items.title: Voodoo Graphics, Rebuilt in Programmable Logic
items.blurb: Starting from a working FPGA 486 CPU, nand2mario spent a month implementing the 3dfx Voodoo Graphics SST-1 in SystemVerilog — triangle rasterization, texture filtering, mipmapping, fog, dithering, the fixed- and floating-point setup interfaces — until Tomb Raider ran with its original 3dfx renderer at 100 MHz on a Xilinx KV260. This is not emulation; it's a re-implementation of the exact rendering pipeline at the logic gate level, recovering the specific visual character of a dead aesthetic era in hardware.

items.title: Four Years to Crack the PS2's Last Secret Chip
items.blurb: DiscoStarslayer chemically decapped the CXP102064 MechaCon — the chip that controlled the PS2's optical drive mechanics and handled Magic Gate memory card and KELF executable decryption — then used optical microscopy to read the die directly. The breakthrough came from what the writeup calls a 'lucky break' during the hacking process, after four years of effort. Twenty-six years after the console launched, one of its last hardware secrets is now open.

items.title: A Mouse With a Human Cortex Performed Better on Memory Tests
items.blurb: Sergiu Pașca's Stanford team genetically modified mice to develop without a cortex or hippocampus, then filled that space with human neural organoids — and the human tissue took hold so thoroughly that nearly half the mouse's brain volume is now human cells. The chimeric mice outperformed mice with no cortex on maze memory tests, meaning the transplanted human tissue is functionally contributing to a living animal's cognition. The mice with no cortex at all, notably, seemed 'fairly normal' otherwise — which raises its own unsettling questions.

facts.fact: Flock's on-device encryption key was stored on the device itself — meaning physical access to the camera was sufficient to decrypt over a million stored vehicle images.
Boston's BPD confirmed with Flock that data-sharing was 'off' before launch — other law enforcement agencies were accessing Boston plate data within three days anyway.
A mouse engineered to develop without a cortex or hippocampus — and then filled with human neural organoids — outperformed normal mice on a spatial memory maze.
The 3dfx Voodoo Graphics SST-1 has been fully reimplemented in SystemVerilog on an FPGA, running Tomb Raider with its original 3dfx renderer at 100 MHz.
Mozilla's benchmark data puts the current open Chinese model capability gap at roughly four months behind frontier proprietary AI, at approximately one-fifth the cost.

art_picks.title: Sans Soleil
art_picks.creator: Chris Marker
art_picks.why: A film structured entirely around the gap between memory, image, and meaning — Marker free-associates across Japan, Guinea-Bissau, Iceland, and the archives of his own mind into something that reads less like a documentary and more like a system for thinking. If you make things that live at the edge of data and feeling, this is the source text.

art_picks.title: Watering a Flower
art_picks.creator: Haruomi Hosono
art_picks.why: The YMO co-founder's ambient solo records — this one especially — treat music the way a generative system treats noise: structured indeterminacy, deep listening, and an obsessive interest in the texture of sound before it becomes song. Made in a 1984 Osaka hospital room, it sounds like nothing else.

art_picks.title: The Propeller Group
art_picks.creator: The Propeller Group
art_picks.why: A Ho Chi Minh City collective who operate simultaneously as an advertising agency and an art practice — treating brand logic, nationalism, and propaganda as raw sculptural material. Their video works are formally gorgeous and structurally sinister, exactly the vibe of systems made visible through their own surface.

events.name: Haruomi Hosono: The Yours Sincerely Tour (with Toro y Moi)
events.venue: Radio City Music Hall, New York
events.why: Tonight only — the 79-year-old YMO co-founder and city pop godfather, rare stateside, with Toro y Moi opening; a living link between Japanese ambient/electronic history and the sounds that quietly rewired Western pop.

events.name: Fallow Frames Biennial
events.why: Artists take over ~20 empty street tree beds across Ridgewood's sidewalks with site-specific installations — infrastructure as canvas, neighborhood as exhibition space, the city's neglected negative space made suddenly loud.

events.name: Shift Ctrl — Tega Brain, Sam Lavigne, Clarissa Redwine & JS Tan
events.why: Four artists and researchers at the center of critical tech/art practice convene at Triple Canopy — the exact overlap of code, culture, and systemic thinking that's in Willem's wheelhouse.

events.name: Arthur Jafa: I Am Tony
events.why: The largest survey of Jafa's career — two floors of montaged image, film, sculpture, and new commissions tracing nearly 40 years of work that treats Black visual culture and media as both subject and system; opens in the newly expanded OMA-designed building.

events.name: The Armory Show 2026
events.why: Not a fair to browse but to use as a map of the current international gallery ecosystem — worth a focused hour or two to read the room on what scenes are consolidating right now, then leave.
